Discounting the companies' schedules for slippage and requiring three months of sustained export gives a 93% chance by 2100 and a median of 2033 (with a 10% chance each of 2029 or earlier and of after 2060), so yellow. label: Advancing: China's EAST tokamak ran stably past the density limit; tritium breeding untested
rationale: In January 2026 a peer-reviewed paper reported that China's EAST tokamak had run stably at up to 1.65 times the density at which tokamak plasmas normally break up (a denser plasma makes more fusion power), the year's one new capability, though reached with a special start-up method rather than in a plasma at fusion-burning conditions; the US laser facility NIF repeated ignition for the 11th time without beating its 2025 record, and private firms reported stronger magnets, laser-fusion fuel targets prepared in hours rather than up to a week, and bigger pulsed-power machines, refinements rather than steps. No step has yet been shown on the two problems this fuel adds, breeding the tritium it burns and materials that survive its neutrons: the facilities to test them are still being designed or built, and Commonwealth Fusion Systems' SPARC, the private machine meant to show net gain from compact magnets, is months behind its magnet schedule. CFS hopes to switch SPARC on in 2027, the international ITER project expects its last core section by mid-2027, and China's BEST tokamak is to finish construction by end-2027 for deuterium-tritium power demonstrations around 2030.

label: Inching: first boron fusion on a private tokamak; plasmas still far below the ~1 billion °C needed
rationale: In September 2026 the Chinese company ENN produced proton-boron fusion reactions in its own tokamak, about 100 million a second, by firing fast protons through a much cooler plasma: far too few for energy gain, and a repeat on a company machine of what a Japanese national laboratory's device had already shown; a peer-reviewed Japanese-American study found that radio-wave heating modestly raises the yield of such beam-driven reactions, and Helion reported 150 million °C in its prototype, along with fusion of ordinary deuterium-tritium fuel rather than the fuels this challenge is about. label: Advancing: first utility-scale enhanced geothermal plant online (33 MW); 10–20 km drilling unproven
rationale: On 30 September 2026 Fervo's Cape Station in Utah became the first utility-scale enhanced geothermal plant in commercial operation, selling 33 MW made by pumping water through artificially fractured hot rock, while a 3 MW pilot in Texas and the UK's first geothermal plant, fed by a 5 km well, also began supplying their grids; the setback came in Germany, where Eavor's closed-loop plant, which circulates water through sealed wells rather than fractured rock, was stopped half-built after cementing failures and rarely exports power. The deep, superhot rock that would make geothermal a fusion-scale alternative is still out of reach: these wells go down about 6 km, and the millimeter-wave drill meant for 10–20 km is at about 1 km by its developer's own account. Fervo expects two more 33 MW units by January 2027 and 400 MW in 2028, and Quaise is drilling a conventional well in Oregon to confirm superhot rock for a 50 MW plant planned as early as 2030.

label: Inching: first commercial enhanced-geothermal plant, per its builder; 10–20 km drilling unproven
rationale: On 30 September 2026 Fervo said its Cape Station in Utah had become the first utility-scale enhanced geothermal plant in commercial operation, selling 33 MW made by pumping water through artificially fractured hot rock, and a 3 MW pilot in Texas and the UK's first geothermal plant, fed by a well over 5 km deep, also began supplying power; in Germany, Eavor's closed-loop plant, which circulates water through sealed wells, stopped its first loop at half its planned well pairs after cementing failures and rarely exports power. The deep, very hot rock that would make geothermal a fusion-scale alternative is still out of reach: Fervo's record well runs about 5.9 km including a 2.3 km horizontal stretch, and Quaise, whose drill melts rock with a millimeter-wave beam and is meant to reach 10–20 km, says only that it is approaching 1 km. Quaise is drilling a conventional well in Oregon to confirm rock near 400 °C for a 50 MW plant planned as early as 2030, and Fervo expects two more 33 MW units by January 2027.

basis.rule: RUBRIC.md §7 (v6): momentum over the 12 months to made_at; first matching row of unknown / Setback / Advancing / Inching / Stalled

advances.what: Fervo declared commercial operation of Cape Station's first 33 MW GeoBlock on 30 Sep 2026 (first power and grid sync 24 Sep, 2026-09-24-fervo-cape-station-first-power), selling power under its PPA: by Fervo's account the first utility-scale enhanced geothermal plant in commercial operation. Not substantive: the ledger's only sources are Fervo's own releases (no grid operator, buyer or independent report), and it is conventionally drilled EGS at ~4-6 km rather than the 10-20 km millimeter-wave/plasma drilling the framework names

Sage Geosystems' 3 MW EGS pilot near San Antonio produced grid-connected power since April 2026 and performed as predicted for >120 days with <10% water loss (reported by Canary Media); small scale, shallow
United Downs, the UK's first geothermal power plant, switched on 26 Feb 2026, drawing ~200 degC water from fractured granite via a >5 km production well (BBC); a national first, not a new capability

Fervo drilled Sawtooth 7 to 19,448 ft (5.9 km) measured depth, i.e. wellbore length including a 7,500 ft (2.3 km) lateral, so the vertical depth is well under 5.9 km and not reported, into 460 degF rock in 21 days, a company drilling-pace record, on track for $5,500/kW Phase II cost; company-reported
Fervo's Blanford appraisal well, drilled in <11 days, measured >555 degF (~290 degC) at ~11,200 ft, its hottest well, with an independent assessment of multi-GW resource potential; company-reported
Mazama's second Newberry well reached 10,350 ft in 15 days (~80% faster than its 2025 well, which created a 331 degC engineered system), drilling toward 400 degC; stated in a funding release

Quaise said its millimeter-wave drilling system was approaching (not at) 1 km at its Texas field site, vs >100 m in 2025: deepest for any non-contact drilling if confirmed; stated in a funding release, company word only. The one in-window number on the framework's named route

Quaise drilled to 100 m with millimeter waves, a record for the method (dated only '2025', so it overlaps the window under §7; it may predate it): the baseline of the 'approaching 1 km' claim; company-reported

GA Drilling's two coordinated NexTitan downhole drive units drilled ~20 m (66 ft) of hard phyllite in 7.5 h at NORCE's Ullrigg test well and powered tools from a downhole turbine generator (April 2026, following a February test of 32,000 lbf thrust, 2026-03-18-ga-drilling-44m-nextitan): a component field test of the deep-drilling system that is to carry GA's plasma drilling, company-reported

setbacks.what: Eavor's Geretsried closed-loop project: Loop #1 stopped at 6 of 12 lateral pairs after cementing failures, ~8.5 MWth vs 64 MWth planned for the full four-loop project, 0.5-1 MWe gross against ~0.5 MWe plant load, so it rarely exports power; Eavor exits the operator role and cut staff from 147 to 80. A technical setback for the closed-loop deep-geothermal route (its December 2025 first power, 2025-12-01-eavor-geretsried-first-power-rv, is therefore not counted as an advance)

basis.prospects: Next: Cape Station's other two 33 MW units by 1 January 2027 and its 400 MW second phase in 2028, most of it contracted to Google. Quaise's first Oregon well, drilled conventionally since July 2026 toward rock near 400 °C, is to confirm the resource for a 50 MW plant as early as 2030; the company says its millimeter-wave drill will not be used there before its hottest wells. Watch for an independently confirmed millimeter-wave or plasma-drilled hole several kilometres deep, and for Cape Station's output over its first year.
basis.change_note: Audit correction (2026-10-28-challenges, rockets-fusion-climate.md, deep-geothermal: two MAJOR findings; README: owner-checked colour change green -> yellow). Status green Advancing -> yellow Inching without new evidence, under rule 8. (1) MAJOR colour: Cape Station's commercial operation rests on Fervo's releases only; prev accepted it as substantive by assuming that the grid operator and PPA buyer corroborate it, which is not an independent report or measurement, and Sage's different pilot does not confirm Cape Station's 33 MW. It is also conventionally drilled EGS, not the framework's named 10-20 km millimeter-wave/plasma drilling. It is now a non-substantive advance; no other advance is substantive (all company-reported, national firsts or component tests), so the verdict is Inching. (2) MAJOR fact: prev's 'these wells go down about 6 km' read Sawtooth 7's 19,448 ft measured depth as vertical depth; now '5.9 km of wellbore including a 2.3 km lateral'; the >5 km depth claim rests on United Downs. Reading (stated as the audit's drilling point is close to a definition question): the challenge is deep geothermal as a mid-term fusion alternative, so deep EGS deployments count as advances on it, while the framework's named route (millimeter-wave/plasma drilling to 10-20 km) is what still blocks. Alternative, drilling-only reading: advances are Quaise's ~1 km and 100 m claims and GA Drilling's field test, none substantive, and Eavor's conventional-drilling failure does not bear on that route: Inching too, so the reading does not change the status. Other fixes: Quaise's Obsidian confirmation well is distinguished in the prospects as conventional drilling; GA Drilling's field test and Quaise's progress foregrounded in the rationale with their attribution. Cross-section findings applied: year-dated '2025' records overlapping the window are counted (Quaise 100 m, as a non-substantive advance) unless legacy (Fervo's 2025 drilling record) or not results (Fervo Series E, IEA cost projection); setbacks sought among all fusion events in the window (only Eavor's bears on geothermal); prospects free of event ids. Oxy's ~6 km GLADE boreholes (April 2025) are before the window: context. Not advances: funding (Fervo IPO and financing, Quaise, Mazama, GA Drilling rounds), PPAs and the Google framework, DOE awards, Quaise's Obsidian plan and well spud, cost estimates (Lazard, IEA). Weighing: advances on the 4-6 km EGS route and incremental drilling progress against one technical setback on the closed-loop route; the setback does not outweigh them. Verdict Inching. Run review: Eavor worded as its first loop stopped at half its planned well pairs, with 64 MWth as the planned four-loop total, not that loop's nameplate.
